From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFP: performance questionnaire and validation protocol request

Claire / Laura — attaching the technical appendix and an initial sample of results (redwood-performance-appendix-A.jsonl). Below is the concise test methodology and the headline numbers we recommend you rely on for procurement comparisons.

Test environment (short):
- Dedicated cluster config used for test: 4 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (single-node), 256GB host RAM, RDMA networking.
- Model variants tested: rw-13b-v2 (float16 baseline), rw-13b-v2-int8 (quantized int8).
- Serving runtime: Redwood Inference serving runtime with dynamic batching and KV prefix cache enabled.
- Load generator: Locust for HTTP/gRPC dispatch + internal token-streaming client to measure per-token latency.
- Prompts: 3 representative templates (short 32-token, medium 128-token, long 512-token). Attached appendix contains the exact prompt seeds used.

Key measurement definitions:
- End-to-end latency: time from request POST to final token emitted (includes network, runtime, model compute, streaming overhead).
- Warm: cache hits for key-value caches and warmed CUDA kernels; measured after sustained warm traffic for 10 minutes.
- Cold: instance just-created + empty KV cache; includes container GPU warm-up and kernel JIT where applicable.

Representative results (512-token generation; average token length ~3 bytes):
- rw-13b-v2-int8 on 1x A100 (single-GPU): p50 = 0.42s, p95 = 1.1s, p99 = 2.0s per request (end-to-end); sustained throughput ~95 tokens/sec (single worker).
- rw-13b-v2-int8 on 4xA100 (our Dedicated node): p50 = 0.11s, p95 = 0.35s, p99 = 0.7s (when dynamic batching active); aggregate sustained throughput ~380 tokens/sec across the node.
- Concurrency scaling: near-linear throughput up to ~32 concurrent requests when batching is effective; beyond that you see queueing and p99 tail growth (we report p99 increases of ~2.5x at >64 concurrent).

Warm vs cold:
- Warm scenario: ~10% lower per-request latency and ~15% higher token throughput vs cold for 512-token cases (due to KV cache hits and kernel warm state).
- Cold starts: Dedicated node (already provisioned) cold-response penalty is dominated by KV miss and kernel JIT: first request penalty ~600-900ms. For Private deployments where we scale from zero, container spin-up + scheduler handoff yields 45—90s median cold start; we recommend pre-warming pools for production.

Batching behavior and cost tradeoffs:
- Dynamic batching reduces per-token compute cost by ~2.8x at typical request-size distributions for rw-13b-v2; we expose max_batch_size and batch_delay_ms as tunables.
- For latency-sensitive endpoints, we tune max_batch_size=8 and batch_delay_ms=6ms as a sweet spot; for throughput/batch-efficient paths we set max_batch_size=64 with batch_delay_ms=20ms.

Autoscale and rollout notes:
- Autoscale triggers: CPU/GPU utilization and request queue length. Typical config: scale-out when avg GPU util > 68% for 30s or queue length > 8, scale-in when util < 35% for 120s.
- Canary runs: we recommend a small canary traffic slice (5–10%) before ramping to 100% for new model variants; auto-fallback is supported to previous stable model.

Artifacts attached:
- redwood-performance-appendix-A.jsonl (sample results with prompt seeds and raw per-request metrics)
- performance-test-plan.xlsx (runbook, Locust scripts pointers, tokenization notes)

If you want, we can provide a short reproducible script (container image) to run the same job inside your environment; that'll require an SSH key to a temporary sandbox or a short-lived API key.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

- Can you confirm the tokenization byte assumptions for the 512-token case (we assume UTF-8 wordpiece; you mentioned ~3 bytes average).
- For Private deployments, the 45—90s spin-up is expected — can you send a suggested pre-warm strategy and an estimated monthly cost delta for keeping a 2-node warm pool in our us-west region?

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute run-through with Rishi next Wednesday to walk through the runbook and, if possible, execute a short live run using your sandbox endpoint. Are you available 11:00–11:30 PT?

If you can attach the reproducible script image or steps to create the sandbox token that would save time.

Claire
